=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:CREDENTIAL_HANDOFF_RE | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The regex for identifying credential handoff prose is not exhaustive and misses common phrasing.
  WHY: Prose such as "Add GH_PAT in acme/other" or "Set GH_PAT as an organization secret" does not match the regex, so the classifier fails to mark the credential step as unrecognised. This can allow a credential step that should require human review to be automatically ticked using this repository's own workflow run proof, even if the secret is configured for another repository or scope.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:CREDENTIAL_SCOPE_FLAG_RE | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The regex for identifying credential scope flags misses flags that appear at the end of a line or are followed by punctuation.
  WHY: A step using `gh secret set GH_PAT --env` or `gh secret set GH_PAT --org,` will not be matched because the regex requires a trailing space or `=`. The step is thus not marked as unrecognised, allowing it to be ticked automatically even when it targets an environment or organization secret.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: scripts/operator_step_issue.py:745-747 (CREDENTIAL_SCOPE_FLAG_RE definition) and scripts/operator_step_issue.py:806-807 (the new `if condition == "credentials" and CREDENTIAL_SCOPE_FLAG_RE.search(text): return None` block) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Prose forms describing organization or environment scope are not classified as unrecognised.
  WHY: Such steps can classify as credentials and be marked met based on a successful workflow run from this repository, potentially closing the tracker although an organization- or environment-scoped secret was not configured.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: Location: CREDENTIAL_REPO_SLUG_RE regex (~line 743). | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
  PROBLEM: Smart quotes (\u201c, \u201d, \u2018, \u2019) bypass the slug guard because the opening-quote character class `[\"']?` only accepts ASCII `"` and `'`.
  WHY: A step like `gh secret set GH_PAT --repo \u201cacme/app\u201d` would not be captured, so the slug check is skipped and the step would classify as credentials for this repository.
  Suggested minimal fix: extend `[\"']?` to `[\"\u201c\u201d\u2018\u2019']?` (or use `[\"\u201c\u201d\u2018\u2019']` on both ends if a closing quote is desired). 1 line.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: lines 745-747, 809 (CREDENTIAL_SCOPE_FLAG_RE and its single use in _observable_condition) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The org/environment-scope guard added by the last run only matches command-line flags; prose describing an organization- or environment-scoped secret passes every guard.
  WHY: The step classifies as `credentials` and `_check_credentials` returns `met` from this repository's own recent successful `review_autofix.yml`/`internal-review.yml`/`security-audit.yml` run, exactly the proof the code comment on lines 745-746 says cannot prove an organisation/environment secret was set.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: line 744 (CREDENTIAL_REPO_SLUG_RE, quote class `[\"']?` added by the last run) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The quoted-slug guard added by the last run accepts only ASCII quotes. A slug wrapped in smart quotes — `gh secret set GH_PAT --repo “acme/app”` — matches nothing.
  WHY: A credentials step targeting another repository, written with typographic quotes in the operator-step instructions, is ticked using this repository's own workflow run as proof and the tracker can close with the other repository's secret still unset. Same bypass for `-R ‘acme/app’` (U+2018/U+2019).
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: line 744, CREDENTIAL_REPO_SLUG_RE | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3
  PROBLEM: Other-repository credentials steps evade the guard via `--repository acme/other`, bare prose (`add GH_PAT in acme/other`), or a `github.com/acme/other/settings/secrets` URL.
  WHY: No flag, no handoff recipient word.
  Suggested minimal fix: add `--repo(?:sitory)?` as the long-flag alternative and a generic `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_/.-])[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+` slug catch-all for credentials text after URL stripping, so any owner/repo pair other than `repo` keeps the step open. Estimated lines changed: 4.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: line 747, CREDENTIAL_SCOPE_FLAG_RE `(?:\s|=)` tail | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
  PROBLEM: A scope flag at end of string or followed by punctuation (`gh secret set GH_PAT --env`, `--env)`, `--org,`) is not matched.
  WHY: Only a following space, tab, newline or `=` fires the guard.
  Suggested minimal fix: replace `(?:\s|=)` with a lookahead `(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])` so the flag itself is enough. Estimated lines changed: 1.
